What the memorandum argues

Four questions the supporting record addresses

These points summarize the author’s stated findings. Readers can review the memorandum and each cited exhibit directly above.

01

Was infrastructure ignored?

The memo cites a December 2022 engineering program documenting nine active work streams involving dams, sewer rehabilitation, water mains, treatment, monitoring, metering, and stormwater mapping.

02

Did tax restraint preclude fiscal strength?

The memo points to the Village’s AA/Stable rating, a 2022 fiscal-stress score of 1.7, a projected 6.51% budget surplus against spending, and a reported 1.7621% levy decrease for 2023–24.

03

Who controlled each project phase?

The memo argues that responsibility should follow control over investigation, design, permitting, grants, borrowing, procurement, construction, change orders, reserves, debt service, and taxation.

04

What decisions were made after 2023?

The memo distinguishes financing authorizations from actual spending and identifies March 2025 water, sewer, and bridge authorizations as decisions of the current Board.
